Driving the next generation of wealth.

Digital assets are redefining how wealth is created, used, and transferred. Since 2018 at Nexo, we have been building the future model of financial wealth - dynamic, accessible, and designed for a new generation of forward-thinking investors.

But technology alone doesn’t drive progress. People do.

We are a team of builders, strategists, analysts, creatives, and operators united by a shared mindset: advancement. We move fast, think long term, and take ownership. We challenge ideas, not people. We value clarity over noise and impact over optics.

What makes Nexo different?

We shape industry trends. We rethink how wealth works and build solutions that reflect that belief.

That requires a certain kind of person.

You will thrive here when you think independently and act decisively, take ownership without waiting for permission, and care deeply about quality, long-term value, and disciplined execution. The people who succeed at Nexo bring analytical depth, sound judgment, and resilience - but also curiosity and the drive to keep improving.

This is an environment for people who want to lead, create, and elevate what already exists. If building what’s next excites you, you’ll feel at home at Nexo.

Official website: nexo.com

Your role:

  • Draft, negotiate, and manage commercial agreements with banks, payment providers, investment firms, vendors, and other regulated partners, including service-level agreements and general terms and conditions.
  • Assess US and international licensing and regulatory requirements for Nexo’s business, and advise how regulatory changes affect our plans.
  • Support US-related initiatives together with the US legal team and external US counsel, including bank, payment provider, investment, and licensing matters.
  • Support negotiations with financial partners from term sheet to signed agreement.
  • Be a go-to legal partner for Compliance, Business, and Product teams, so legal and regulatory requirements are considered early.
  • Support the legal setup of new products and programs as they arise.
  • Turn recurring questions into templates, playbooks, and self-service guidance, including AI-assisted workflows.
  • Work closely with colleagues across the legal team and share coverage when they are away.
  • Handle ad-hoc legal queries from across Nexo.
  • Report to the Head of Legal and work with regional counsels, external counsel, and regulators.
  • Share knowledge with colleagues and, over time, help develop junior team members.

What makes you stand out:

  • Master’s degree in law (LLB, JD or equivalent) and a strong academic record.
  • 5+ years of experience in-house or in a law firm, advising US-regulated entities such as banks, payment companies, fintechs, or investment advisers.
  • Strong US law exposure, with a focus on commercial agreements, regulatory matters, or both.
  • Experience negotiating with banks, payment providers, or other regulated financial institutions.
  • Working knowledge of US financial regulation, such as licensing, AML, consumer protection, or securities and investment adviser rules.
  • Experience supporting product or program launches is a plus.
  • Crypto and blockchain experience is a plus, not a requirement. We’ll help you build it.
  • Ability to turn regulatory risk into practical, business-friendly solutions.
  • Strong drafting and negotiation skills, and excellent written and spoken English.
  • A hands-on mindset: comfortable drafting, negotiating, advising, and getting things done without a large support team.
  • Comfortable using AI tools to speed up drafting, research, and contract review.
  • Ability to work independently on complex, cross-jurisdictional projects in a fast-paced environment, and as a team player who shares knowledge so no single person is a bottleneck.
  • Strong analytical, prioritization, and multi-tasking skills, with attention to detail.

Nexo benefits:

  • Competitive and rewarding remuneration package.
  • Annual performance-based bonuses.
  • Comprehensive Learning Hub for continuous growth.
  • Hybrid work model: primarily office-based with scheduled home office flexibility.
  • A dynamic and inspiring environment with cutting-edge projects.
  • Career development opportunities in a global leader driving the next generation of wealth.
  • Customizable personal benefits package.
  • Wellness benefits include additional health insurance, all-access sports cards, team-wide sports activities, standing desks, and blue light glasses.
  • Free parking with a designated space, free electric bikes, and public transportation cards.
  • Fresh fruits, snacks, and a well-stocked office kitchen.
  • Regular department team buildings and company-wide team buildings.
descriptions.job-08t6qv1:
DRW is a diversified trading firm with over 3 decades of experience bringing sophisticated technology and exceptional people together to operate in markets around the world. We value autonomy and the ability to quickly pivot to capture opportunities, so we operate using our own capital and trading at our own risk.

Headquartered in Chicago with offices throughout the U.S., Canada, Europe, and Asia, we trade a variety of asset classes including Fixed Income, ETFs, Equities, FX, Commodities and Energy across all major global markets. We have also leveraged our expertise and technology to expand into three non-traditional strategies: real estate, venture capital and cryptoassets.

We operate with respect, curiosity and open minds. The people who thrive here share our belief that it’s not just what we do that matters–it's how we do it. DRW is a place of high expectations, integrity, innovation and a willingness to challenge consensus.

UP (Unified Platform) consolidates data and technologies into a comprehensive solution, accelerating time to market. Optimizing decision-making and research, our platform simplifies implementing new ideas, enhancing our competitive edge. We work from high-level requirements where programmers are expected to gain an intimate understanding of the business. We strive for an environment where developers have the autonomy to pursue business solutions without arbitrary management constraints. We are a group of polyglots and technologists always seeking to find the right tool for each problem. Broadly, the development teams at DRW believe in rapid deployment and feedback, automated testing, and cohesive, transparent, lightly coupled service architectures.

The Platform Services team builds self-service platform products that simplify how development teams interact with infrastructure. Its goal is to let teams focus on delivering business value rather than on platform integrations and infrastructure complexity. Examples include: 

Access Management – Work towards a single source of truth for who can do what at DRW. Simplify engineering's approach to Identity and Access Management (IAM) by providing a platform that can be used to manage access across DRW's proprietary and third-party systems. 

Limit Monitoring – Create a platform for defining and monitoring firmwide trading limits across domains like Risk, Treasury, and Compliance. 

Data Tables – Provide a best-of-breed service for managing lightweight datasets, with built-in support for temporal (point-in-time) data, access controls, APIs, and front end. 

Usage – Normalize the collection, storage, and presentation of usage data to provide insight into how services and data are being used and why. 

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will define, develop, and own services that form the foundation of DRW's Unified Platform. 

Key Responsibilities: 

  • Architect and deliver complex features end-to-end with minimal oversight. 
  • Turn high-level requirements into solutions, drawing on a deep understanding of the business. 
  • Maintain a constant focus on testing, reliability, scalability, and maintainability. 
  • Design systems, model data, and write code across a variety of languages and technologies. 
  • Evolve legacy code alongside greenfield development. 
  • Learn and promote new technologies with a focus on best practices. 
  • Engage in on-call and production support activities. 
  • Contribute to system and architecture design discussions. 
  • Challenge ideas and participate in defining the path forward. 

Required Qualifications: 

  • 7+ years of experience in server-side development using major programming languages such as Java, Ruby, Python, Clojure, or C#. 
  • Strong understanding of system and architecture design principles, especially in the context of distributed systems. 
  • Ability to own projects, define requirements, and lead their development. 
  • Excellent problem-solving skills, with the capacity to work on both software development and support tasks. 
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills. 

Desirable Qualifications: 

  • Experience with Platform as a Service (PaaS) and the transformation of services into products. 
  • Experience with IAM concepts such as RBAC/ABAC, OAuth 2.0/OIDC, or SCIM. 
  • Experience with temporal data modeling and designing APIs consumed by other teams. 
  • Experience building real-time or event-driven systems.

Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

The Crypto Risk team's mission is to identify, assess, and mitigate risk across Robinhood Crypto's products, operations, and platforms, protecting customers and the firm as the business scales. We work to deliver an excellent end-customer experience while upholding the safety and soundness of the business, so Robinhood can keep expanding access to crypto responsibly. The team partners with engineering, product, compliance, crypto operations, and enterprise risk to keep a consistent view of risk across the organization. It's an exciting time to join as we launch new products and expand our crypto offering!

As a Risk Specialist, you will support the execution of our crypto risk management program, partnering closely with Crypto Risk leadership to monitor, assess, and report on risk across the business. You will play a hands-on role in building and running operational risk management, with a particular focus on technical and product risk. Day to day, you will assess new products and business changes for risk, run risk and control self-assessments, and prepare reporting for governance forums. You will translate technical risks into clear terms for colleagues outside engineering and work closely with partner teams across the business. Your work will help us keep pace with new launches while protecting customers and the firm!

This role is based in our New York, NY and Menlo Park, CA offices, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

  • Facilitate Technical Risk Assessments (TRAs) and product risk assessments for new and existing crypto products, features, and business changes: document and assess risks and controls in collaboration with engineering and product owners.
  • Analyze incident and issue data to identify recurring root causes, control weaknesses and systemic themes; lead or support retrospectives on material events and translate findings into actionable risk insights for leadership.
  • Mature the operational loss tracking process, including loss definitions, intake, taxonomy, linkage to incidents and issues, and trend reporting.
  • Manage the issue management lifecycle, from identification and prioritization through remediation tracking and closure, ensuring issues are handled and escalated appropriately.
  • Perform and refresh Risk and Control Self-Assessments (RCSAs) and support Business Impact Analyses.
  • Monitor, refine and develop key risk indicators (KRIs), and prepare risk reporting for governance forums, including risk committee and board materials and escalations.Translate technical risks into clear, actionable terms for non-engineering stakeholders.
  • Translate technical risks into clear, actionable terms for non-engineering partners.
  • Partner with engineering, product, compliance, crypto operations, and enterprise risk teams to maintain a consistent view of risk across the organization.

What you bring

  • 5+ years of experience in operational risk, enterprise risk management, or technology risk at a regulated financial services or crypto/fintech firm. (US-based ERM experience is preferred).
  • Hands-on experience facilitating risk assessments (RCSA, technology or product risk assessments, process risk assessments), including working directly with business, product and engineering owners.
  • Experience designing, running or materially contributing to business continuity or disaster recovery exercises, including scenario design, facilitation and after action reporting.
  • Experience performing root cause analysis or thematic analysis across incidents, with the ability to identify patterns and systemic issues from operational data.
  • Deep understanding of risk management methodologies, including risk taxonomies, control design, KRIs and issue management.
  • Technical exposure and comfort working in a technical environment, with the ability to read engineering design documents and incident post mortems and extract the risk. A software engineering background is not required.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical colleagues and present risk findings to stakeholders across the organization.
  • Detail oriented, with a proactive, independent approach to identifying and addressing risk.

Bonus points

  • Direct experience in the cryptocurrency industry, with familiarity with crypto products, custody, and blockchain fundamentals.
  • A computer science or engineering degree, especially if you have built a career in risk, compliance, or another non-engineering role.
  • Experience building or operating an operational loss event program
  • Exposure to third party and vendor risk management, particularly for critical technology or custody providers.
  • Familiarity with operational resilience regulatory expectations such as NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500, DORA or MiCA.
  • Experience with governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) tools such as LogicGate or similar platforms.
  • Analytical background with knowledge of SQL, Python, or a BI tool.

Developed using the latest technology, Ripple Treasury helps empower organizations on their path to strategic treasury, by enabling total visibility into their cash, liquidity, payments and financial risk management.

As a Professional Services Consultant, you are the critical link between our cutting- edge technology and the real-world financial goals of our global clients. Prime Intellect is building the open superintelligence stack: the infrastructure frontier AI labs build internally, made available to every ambitious AI team.

 

Our platform, Lab, unifies compute, environments, evaluations, secure sandboxes, high-performance training, and deployment into one full-stack system for post-training at frontier scale - from SFT and RL to tool use, agent workflows, and continuously improving production models. The next generation of AI companies, enterprises, and research teams do not just need more GPUs. They need the ability to turn their own workflows, tools, data, and feedback loops into superintelligence they own.

We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of frontier research, real infrastructure, and go-to-market for a category that does not fully exist yet.

Role Impact

Computer-use agents must understand changing interfaces, maintain intent over long workflows, recover from mistakes, manage permissions and side effects, and know when an outcome is actually complete. You will build post-training and evaluation systems for multimodal agents operating browsers, desktops, and cross-application workflows. The work is grounded in an active external program. The research challenge is turning real workflows and traces into environments, rewards, and experiments that produce reliable improvement.

Responsibilities

Applied Research at Prime

We turn a workflow into tasks, environments, evaluations, and reward signals, run post-training experiments against real baselines, and deploy what works. When a result looks good, we find out whether the gain came from the model or from the data, harness, inference, or infrastructure. The reusable parts become shared research, open-source systems, and product capabilities.

Every Applied Research role is externally facing. Most researchers work directly with customers, users, or research partners while maintaining a substantive research agenda.

Representative early problems

  • Build long-horizon computer-use environments from real workflows while preventing shortcuts, leakage, and unsafe side effects.

  • Train agents to recover from interface changes, partial failures, and ambiguous intermediate states instead of restarting or silently drifting.

  • Develop evaluations that distinguish genuine completion from plausible-looking behavior, including correctness, efficiency, permissions, and appropriate escalation.

What you will own

  • Multimodal environments built from partner workflows, demonstrations, tools, interface state, and outcome criteria.

  • Browser, desktop, and cross-application agents with reliable sandbox and boundary enforcement.

  • Training and evaluation from demonstrations, interventions, production failures, synthetic tasks, and verifiable outcomes.

  • Experiments on recovery and generalization across applications, layouts, permissions, and deployment contexts.

Requirements

  • Relevant experience: multimodal agents, computer use, browser or desktop automation, RL, imitation learning, HCI, embodied agents, or long-horizon agent evaluation.

  • Hands-on experience building and debugging model-training, post-training, agent, evaluation, or closely adjacent experimental loops.

  • Strong experimental judgment: meaningful baselines, careful trace inspection, clear failure attribution, and a willingness to change direction when the evidence changes.

  • Strong Python and the ability to build artifacts that other researchers and engineers can run, inspect, and extend.

  • Comfort owning ambiguous problems and keeping partners and teammates current as you resolve them.

Evidence of exceptional work

We value publications, open-source systems, benchmarks, and shipped products as evidence of exceptional work. Show us something difficult you built, what failed, and how the evidence changed your approach.

  • Cash Compensation Range of $150-300k + equity incentives

  • Flexible Work (San Francisco, New York, London, or remote)

About the Role

The Transaction Reporting Analyst is a critical role responsible for the operational integrity of DriveWealth's regulatory trade reporting. This role is responsible for performing the Firm's front-line supervisory reviews: working exception reports generated across trading, order handling, and FINRA trade reporting activity; investigating and documenting findings; and escalating issues to the appropriate supervisor or principal in line with the Firm's Written Supervisory Procedures (WSPs).
This is an operational, evidence-driven function. It requires the ability to read and apply the Firm's supervisory procedures, work efficiently through exception queues, spot patterns that need escalation, and maintain clean, examiner-ready records of every review performed. Prior experience with order/trade surveillance systems, exception-based reporting, or retail brokerage operations is highly desirable but not required. 

What You’ll Do

  • Perform daily/periodic Level 1 supervisory reviews of assigned exception reports (e.g., trade and order exceptions, CAT/CAIS/TRF/ORF/TRACE supervisory report exceptions)
  • Investigate flagged items to determine root cause, gather supporting evidence, and reach a documented conclusion
  • Clear reviewed items from the queue and log the review, findings, and disposition in the Firm's designated system of record
  • Track issues through to resolution and confirm that corrective action was taken and evidenced
  • Identify recurring exception patterns and recommend process, control, or system improvements to reduce false positives and close gaps
  • Maintain organized, accurate records to support compliance testing, internal audit, and regulatory examinations
  • Assist in gathering facts and documentation in response to regulatory inquiries or exams
  • Partner with Engineering and Brokerage Operations to improve the automation and reliability of monitoring workflows.
  • Stay current on the FINRA rules and internal procedures governing the reviews performed

You Bring

  • Minimum 3+ years of experience in a compliance, supervision, operations, or analytical role, preferably at a broker-dealer or other financial services firm
  • Direct exposure to FINRA trade reporting (CAT/CAIS/TRF/ORF/TRACE), SEC Rule 605 and 606 reporting or equivalent regulatory transaction reporting is a plus.

  • A track record of ownership and disciplined execution in high-stakes, deadline-driven environments.
  • The ability to prioritize effectively and know when to escalate versus resolve independently.
  • Strong written communication skills — able to document findings and escalations clearly and defensibly
  • Impeccable integrity, sound judgment, high attention to detail and a deep respect for risk, control, and regulatory obligations.
  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Business, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

  • Active Series 7 required
